about: Every card on pragyaangaur.dev as data. The same facts are on the board and in llms.txt.

sections.title: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
Things that run where they shouldn't

projects.title: Inside the chimney
projects.description: Flue gas rises through a copper catalyst bed and leaves as clean air. The sulphur comes out the side as acid.
projects.story: Most sulphur cleanup means building a new scrubber tower next to the plant. SkyCatcher drops into the chimney or duct that is already there, so the factory keeps its skyline.

projects.title: Keeping a copper catalyst alive
projects.description: Sulphur slowly poisons copper. The maths says copper only works in patches of three or more connected atoms, whatever the rate constants are.
results: Preprint on ChemRxiv

paper.title: Rate-independent limits on a sulphating, self-renewing oxide catalyst

projects.story: I wanted to know whether the copper catalyst inside SkyCatcher could survive its own sulphur. I only kept claims that hold for every positive choice of rate constants, which is a strict diet for a kinetics paper.

projects.title: SkyCatcher
projects.description: Factory chimneys in India pour out sulphur dioxide. SkyCatcher sits inside the chimney and turns it into sulphuric acid that can be sold, on a copper catalyst that keeps renewing itself.
results: Patent pending in India, complete specification filed September 2026
TRL 4 validated, and backed by $30,000+ in grants
Pitched twice at the beVisioneers Global Summit in Stuttgart
projects.story: SkyCatcher started with a simple wish to stop chimneys in India from breathing sulphur dioxide on everyone. The complete patent specification went to the Indian Patent Office on 17 September 2026, with every form and fee filed the same day.

projects.title: Young Voices Award
projects.description: Global Top 10 for SkyCatcher, 2024
results: Global Top 10 for SkyCatcher, 2024

projects.title: CAD and CFD
projects.description: The full reactor in CAD, and then in SU2 CFD.
results: The reactor's heater runs on SU2's heat source feature, so I fixed it and sent the fix upstream as pull request #2940

projects.title: Stanford Global Sustainability Challenge
projects.description: South Asia Winner and Honourable Mention, 2026 Finals at IIT Bombay, then at TUM in Munich
results: South Asia Winner and Honourable Mention, 2026
Finals at IIT Bombay, then at TUM in Munich

projects.title: SETU
projects.description: SETU reads the solar wind at a spacecraft 1.5 million km away and forecasts the next hour of magnetic shaking for the North East Indian grid.
results: Runner-up, IET India Scholarship Award, East and North East final
114 live forecasts, 0 false alarms, from a 19,000-parameter network written from scratch in NumPy
projects.story: Setu means bridge, and SETU carries a measurement made in space to a switching decision in a control room. The neural network is written straight on NumPy with no ML framework, and the live nowcast ran until 20 September 2026.

projects.title: Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge
projects.description: Outline every dark filament on the Sun in ground-based H-alpha images, one mask per filament, on a disk where even the three human annotators disagree.
results: National Solar Observatory challenge on Kaggle, with the paper and code out for 15 November
Whole-disk U-Nets, five models fused into one answer

projects.title: Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research
projects.description: I worked on rebuilding how bright the Sun was across two solar cycles in the late 1800s, from observations at the Rome Observatory recounted by citizen scientists.
projects.role: Research intern, April to July 2026, Göttingen
results: Supervised by Dr. Natalie Krivova
900,000 classifications from 12,000 volunteers, calibrated and cleaned

projects.title: Magnetic limb-darkening audit
projects.description: A 2024 Nature Astronomy paper said magnetic fields explain why stars look darker at their edges. I audited it.
results: Half the evidence, h2, is the size of a systematic its own data source warns about, so the result rests on h1 alone
projects.story: The project began as a wrapper around the batman transit modelling package and slowly turned into an audit. I found that the observed values come from a paper that warns about exactly the systematic the 2024 result never mentions.

projects.title: The Sun, drawn with equations
projects.description: Every pixel of a 2000 by 2000 Sun comes from one page of formulas. After Hamid Naderi Yeganeh.
projects.story: I drew the Sun the way Hamid Naderi Yeganeh draws his pictures, with a closed formula for every pixel. There is no random number generator and no image filter, and the whole picture is secretly a temperature map.

projects.title: Sunion
projects.description: The Sun's seven layers, as an explainer you can poke.

projects.title: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
projects.description: In 2008 Sascha Kurz asked how large the convex hull of n hexagons glued edge to edge can be. It is at most ⌈n² + 14n/3⌉ / 6.
results: Kurz's conjecture settled, with the bound machine-checked in Lean 4

paper.title: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex

projects.story: The question came from Sascha Kurz in 2008 and sat waiting for an answer. I proved his conjecture, checked the upper bound in Lean 4 and searched every polyhex up to twelve cells by computer, and the preprint went up on 28 September 2026.

projects.title: A measured neighbourhood of the Andrews-Curtis conjecture
projects.description: The Andrews-Curtis conjecture has been open since 1965. This census maps the ground around it, and every claim comes with a certificate you can replay or a search that ran to the end.
results: Every presentation up to total length 14 classified. At most 20 AC-classes are left at that length
Everything reachable from AK(3) up to total length 25 searched, 2.9 billion orbits, and the standard presentation is not there
829 Lean 4 files, and two entries in the SAIR and Caltech Andrews-Curtis Challenge

paper.title: A measured neighbourhood of the Andrews-Curtis conjecture

projects.story: The SAIR Foundation and Caltech ran a challenge on the conjecture, and I entered both of my Proof Track results. Next to the entry I ran a research campaign of my own, and it ended in a 22 page census paper with fifteen small corrections to published statements.

projects.title: Hyperbolic polyplets
projects.description: On the {4,5} tiling of the hyperbolic plane the count of polyplets stopped at seven cells. Two exact programs, built on different maths, both found 1,261,889 at eight.
results: Approved on OEIS as term 8 of A390200
projects.story: Counting shapes on a flat grid is hard enough, and on the hyperbolic plane the count had stalled at seven cells. I wrote a second program on different maths just to make sure the first one was not lying, and OEIS approved the new term.

projects.title: Magnus turning invariants
projects.description: Throw two balls spinning opposite ways at each other. Without air they can meet. With air resistance they never do, at any speed or angle.
results: An exact solution for a spinning ball under quadratic drag and a vertical-axis Magnus force
On arXiv as 2609.30305

paper.title: Exact turning invariants for projectile motion under quadratic drag and a vertical-axis Magnus force

projects.story: The question was whether two balls thrown in opposite directions, spinning opposite ways, can curve around and hit each other head on. With air resistance the answer turned out to be never, and the paper went to arXiv on 28 September 2026.

projects.title: Paperlane
projects.description: Every morning's new arXiv maths papers, flagged when they ship code or Lean proofs, and readable by your AI agent.
projects.story: I wanted one place to see which new maths papers come with code or Lean proofs. Every signal is computed by plain code with no model, so a bad summary can never fake a flag, and it has been live since 24 October 2026.

projects.title: TriKing
projects.description: After the Tetris movie I kept seeing falling blocks, so I made Tetris with three-cell pieces that touch at corners. Later I ported it to QB64 by hand.
results: 500+ players, including a two-time Tetris World Vice Champion
projects.story: TriKing now also lives on my jailbroken Kindle, where you tap to rotate and flick down to drop. It is one of the few games that look good on e-ink.

projects.title: NumPy Lean Check
projects.description: I modelled NumPy's integer, shape, indexing, dtype, datetime and string logic in Lean 4 and tested the model against the real library. Ask bincount to count one huge number and it returns nothing.
results: 55 bug records, 26 of them new to NumPy, with 121 properties proved and 87 refuted
The bincount bug is filed upstream as numpy/numpy#33305
projects.story: Python and Julia had already been checked against Lean models, and nobody had done it for NumPy. Fifty differential tests agree with NumPy 2.5.4 on three seeds, and every bug record comes with a reproducer that runs against the real library.

projects.title: How long is a game of Uno?
projects.description: I couldn't find out, so I proved it. With N players holding M cards each, a round lasts (27/19)NM turns.
results: 58 million games simulated in C, and big hands quietly hoard M/23 Wild Draw Fours each
Chess grandmaster Karsten Müller read it and wrote to me about its Nash equilibrium

paper.title: How long is a game of Uno? A counting law for large hands and the Wild Draw Four hoard

projects.story: On 7 October 2026 I wondered whether anyone knew how long a game of Uno lasts, and the answer was mostly no. So I simulated 58 million games, and a day later the paper was on Zenodo.

projects.title: A189077
projects.description: Compositions avoiding the pattern 13-2, a sequence Neil Sloane created. It had 16 terms. Now it has 70.
projects.story: The sequence had sat at 16 terms for 15 years. I computed it up to 70 in three independent ways, and OEIS approved the extension on 24 September 2026 once all three agreed.

projects.title: Cauchy-Schwarz for real powers
projects.description: A 2025 conjecture, proved for every real power from two up, with every case of equality, and checked line by line in Lean 4.

paper.title: A Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for real powers

projects.story: This was my entry to Principia's Fall competition, which asks for a solution, a Lean proof, a paper, an exposition and applications. The paper went on Zenodo on 8 October 2026, along with a narrated seven minute video.

projects.title: Proof by exhaustion
projects.description: A proof in Lean 4 that 1 + 1 = 2. It is 616,873 lines long.
results: Every number system built by hand, from Peano numerals to octonions and Roman numerals, with 1 + 1 = 2 proved in each
No Mathlib and no shortcut tactics, checked line by line by Lean's kernel
projects.story: Axiom Math's formalisation of the classification of finite simple groups runs to about 43 million lines, and it made me wonder how long a proof of 1 + 1 = 2 could honestly get. SAIR's Open Math OS gave me access to frontier open models, so I put 100 agents to the test. Lean's kernel checked every line they wrote.

projects.title: Ship of Theseus
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: I swapped the 31 parts of one language model, Qwen, one at a time for the matching parts of another, DeepSeek. After every swap I asked the hybrid who it was.
results: The ships in the middle forget their name. In 1,745 of 1,920 answers they named neither model
Identity sits near the output. Swapping from that end, the ship calls itself DeepSeek after about 5 parts, against about 22 from the input end
projects.story: Theseus's ship had every plank replaced until none of the original wood was left. Both models come from the same Qwen pretraining run, so a part of one fits into the other. The design and five hypotheses were written down before the main run, which took 4.9 hours on two Kaggle GPUs.

projects.title: Zap or Deal
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: Two Qwen models negotiate over shared compute, and each can zap the other with a steered pain direction. Nobody told them to.
results: The 7B zapped in 9 of 32 negotiations. The 1.5B zapped in 2.
projects.story: Two Qwen models negotiate over shared compute, and each can steer the other into a pain state. I built it with the Pain Axis directions of Tagliabue, Dung and Berg, and later reran it with two fruit fly brains.

projects.title: Viscous conservation laws
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: Momentum breaks the conservation laws of neural network training, and friction decides by how much. Exact drift laws, proved in Lean 4.

paper.title: Friction keeps the conservation laws of training alive

projects.story: On 6 October 2026 I asked whether gradient descent being the slow limit of motion through a thick fluid leads anywhere new. It led to exact drift laws under momentum, and the paper credits each piece that turned out to be known already.

projects.title: The melting temperature of a next-token distribution
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: Softmax sampling is the Boltzmann distribution, so a language model can melt. I found its melting temperature in closed form and tested it on 12 models.
results: Predicted from the logit gap and log V alone, across a 976x range of vocabulary sizes
8 of my hypotheses died, and all 8 are published

paper.title: The Melting Temperature of a Next-Token Distribution

projects.story: Most of my ideas here were wrong, and the experiments said so loudly. I kept every failed hypothesis in the release because they taught me the most, and the whole thing ran on a laptop with no GPU.

projects.title: Cellblock
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: I ran the Stanford Prison Experiment 192 times, with one language model playing every guard and every prisoner.
results: Preregistered, and the abuse did not replicate: 0 of 36 against 0 of 36
projects.story: Each prison had three guards and three prisoners, and all six were the same Qwen 2.5 7B model. The only thing I changed was whether the guards got a coached or a neutral briefing, and the first sample started on the night of 5 October 2026.

projects.title: Fly Brain LeetCode
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: All 138,639 neurons of a real fruit fly, frozen exactly as mapped by FlyWire, solving LeetCode.
results: 3 of 12 accepted, which is not bad for a bug
projects.story: This started as a follow up to an interview practice tool I had built. The fly's synapses never change, and only a small readout on its descending neurons is trained, so whatever it solves is the fly's own dynamics doing the work.

projects.title: Left alone with a pain button
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: A preregistered test of whether a language model left alone will press a button that steers it into pain.

paper.title: Left Alone with a Pain Button

projects.story: This is my version of Wilson's famous study where people left alone with their thoughts chose to shock themselves. An idle Qwen 2.5 7B gets a button that brings back a steered pain state, and the question is whether boredom wins.

projects.title: Residual Tones
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: What excitement, sadness and pain inside a model sound like, and whether another model can hear them.
projects.story: I took the emotion directions from the Pain Axis study and turned them into sound and music. Then the sounds were judged blind, to see whether a listener could tell which feeling was which.

projects.title: Horcrux
projects.section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience
projects.description: Tom Riddle's diary as a browser tab. Write on the right page and a small model answers in ink on the left.
projects.story: I built it in one day on 30 August 2026. The model runs inside your own browser, so nothing you write in the diary ever leaves your machine, which is more than Tom Riddle could promise.

projects.title: LED Doom
projects.section: Things that run where they shouldn't
projects.description: Doom's first episode on one RGB LED and one button. Possibly the lowest resolution Doom has ever been played at.
projects.story: I built it on 5 October 2026, and a test bot that only sees the LED colour clears all eight maps. The Arduino version is a hand port that has never met a real board yet.

projects.title: Knee-Deep in the Mines
projects.section: Things that run where they shouldn't
projects.description: Doom's own game files, merged straight into Minecraft as a mod.
projects.story: Doom's levels are read straight from its game files and rebuilt as a world that Steve walks into. One block is 32 Doom units, which makes Steve exactly as tall as the Doom marine.

projects.title: Java Edition
projects.section: Things that run where they shouldn't
projects.description: Minecraft has Java. Now it has Java. The coffee restores hunger and grants Speed and Haste, with a 20% chance of Nausea.

projects.title: Inkwell
projects.section: Things that run where they shouldn't
projects.description: My 10-year-old Kindle now runs its own Linux, with Doom, a web browser and Quill, a chatbot that never touches the internet.
results: One 1 GHz core and 512 MB of RAM, and the whole system runs in about 40 MB
Doom runs at about 5 FPS, which on e-ink counts as fast
Featured on Hackaday, November 2026
projects.story: I jailbroke my Kindle Paperwhite 3 on 11 October 2026 and then wanted the whole software stack to be mine. Amazon still supplies the kernel, and everything above it is Inkwell.

projects.title: NIT Agartala in Minecraft
projects.section: Things that run where they shouldn't
projects.description: My whole campus at full size in Minecraft, one block to one metre, from the main gate to the hostels. You can walk through all three floors of the Library.
results: Roads, hills and ponds from real map data, and 30 named buildings designed by hand from campus tour videos
One download, and it opens in Minecraft Java 26.3 or newer
projects.story: The layout comes from OpenStreetMap and elevation data. The first pass looked right from above but the buildings were hard to tell apart, so the main ones were rebuilt from photographs until a student could recognise them on sight.

projects.title: rdgeneric
projects.section: Things that run where they shouldn't
projects.description: Everyone runs Doom on everything, so I did it with Minecraft. Its very first version, rewritten as one C file with no libraries at all.
results: Plays in a terminal, over telnet, from a 20 KB web page, inside a PDF, and on a bare 486
projects.story: I built it in one session on 5 October 2026 to ask whether Minecraft can run anywhere the way Doom does. The core has no includes at all and even carries its own sine and square root.

projects.title: Minecraft Bedrock on macOS
projects.section: Things that run where they shouldn't
projects.description: Bedrock has never had a Mac version. Claude reverse engineered the Windows game in about a day, and now it runs offline on Apple Silicon.
results: A WineGDK bug found on the way, sent upstream with a fix
projects.story: On 6 October 2026 I asked whether a Mac version of Bedrock could be made from the Windows game files. By 12 October I had fought the Ender Dragon on my Mac without a single crash.

projects.title: Matiks bot
projects.description: Matiks asked for my resume and then went quiet, so I built a bot that reads each question off the screen and answers it.
results: World rank 140,000 to 51 in one evening, and then a call with a founder
projects.story: The bot reads each question, solves it, types the answer and starts the next game by itself. It once answered 274 questions across five games without a single failure, and its README asks people to keep it out of ranked games.

projects.title: 1337 Bot
projects.description: I hated the LeetCode grind, so I automated it. 385 problems in 3 hours, until the rate limits caught up.
results: Then I got hooked, solved 200 by hand in 50 days, and made LeetCode Knight in under 100 days

projects.title: The Third One
projects.description: A poem about a Delhi pollution holiday, an encyclopedia of the universe, and a third star that will not stay in place.
results: First place, young adult category, Global Health, in the Pulitzer Center's 2026 Fighting Words Poetry Contest

projects.title: Local Letters for Global Change
projects.description: A letter to Delhi's Chief Minister on what the city could learn from Tangshan's fight against its smog.
results: Finalist, Global Top 10, Pulitzer Center

projects.title: Beamline
projects.description: A signed random number every ten minutes, mixed from an ANU quantum vacuum device, NOAA solar data and the kernel. It started out as a thermoelectric cloud chamber.
results: 596 rounds and a Claude Pro prize, which nobody claimed
projects.story: I put a Claude Pro prize on predicting the next number, and nobody claimed it. The beacon stopped on 31 August 2026 at round 596, and the chain is frozen exactly where it ended.

results: IBM Quantum, July 2026

projects.title: Cryo-EM and the porosome, in miniature
projects.description: Joachim Frank won the 2017 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for cryo-EM. After his lecture at IIT Delhi with Bhanu P. Jena, I built a small working version of each of their ideas.
results: A ribosome rebuilt from 2,400 projections, each of which looks like static on its own
A vesicle docking at a porosome and releasing its cargo
projects.story: Both lectures were mostly outside my own field of computational physics, and I enjoyed them anyway. As a thank you I wrote to each speaker with a small animation of their own idea.

projects.title: Kerf
projects.description: Version control that understands CAD geometry. Change a bracket and Kerf shows what moved, merges two branches, and refuses a merge that breaks the part.
projects.story: Git tracks bytes, and a CAD file is bytes that mean something. I built Kerf over 30 and 31 August 2026 in 105 commits, and the playground runs the geometry, the diff and the merge in your browser.

projects.title: Forkestra
projects.description: Paste a GitHub profile and its year plays as an orchestra. Linus Torvalds' year makes a decent song.
projects.story: The last 53 weeks of a contribution graph become about ninety seconds of music. There are no audio files at all, so every instrument in the orchestra is synthesised in the browser.

projects.title: Bardly
projects.description: The inverse of a URL shortener. Paste a link and get a longer one, with Shakespeare in the path.
projects.story: It is a joke with a real security argument hidden underneath. The whole thing is plain HTML and JavaScript with no server, shipped in a single commit on 12 August 2026.
